\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

The text on which large language models are trained increasingly contains their own outputs.
As synthetic content proliferates across the web, a recursive loop emerges: models trained on web corpora ingest text generated by earlier models, and their outputs feed into the next generation's training data \cite{shumailov2024_nature,alemohammad2024_mad}.
This model$\to$data$\to$model cycle is no longer hypothetical; it is already occurring in the wild. Yet whether the recursive generation depth of a text can be estimated from its statistical properties remains unstudied, a question that matters because first-generation synthetic text may be benign or even beneficial for training, while deeply recursive text drives the distributional collapse that degrades model quality \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}.
In this work, we focus on the 1--1.5B parameter regime under \emph{controlled full-replacement chains}, where each generation fully replaces the prior training set, isolating the depth variable. Real-world contamination typically involves partial mixing (accumulation), where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions; the full-replacement setting provides an upper bound on depth signal strength, and we discuss implications for accumulation settings in \S\ref{sec:discussion}.

Existing tools address adjacent but distinct problems.
Binary detectors \cite{binoculars2024,fast_detectgpt2024,diveye2026} collapse all depths $d \geq 1$ into a single category; watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} requires proactive embedding.
The model collapse literature \cite{shumailov2024_nature,dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails} assumes depth is known a priori; \citet{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse} filter synthetic data via binary detection without distinguishing depths.
No existing method estimates the ordinal recursive generation depth of a text passage from its content alone (Figure~\ref{fig:problem}).

We find that recursive generation leaves quantifiable statistical fingerprints in text, and these fingerprints are \textbf{consistent in direction but scale-dependent in magnitude} across the three model families and three decoding strategies studied.
Specifically, the perplexity tail feature family (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) and surprisal variance emerge as dominant depth indicators, with group-level dominance robust across all 9 model--strategy configurations and three importance measures.
Following the tradition of benchmark-driven empirical studies in NLP, our contribution centers on task formalization and systematic empirical characterization rather than algorithmic novelty; the convergence of four classifiers within 0.8\,pp (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}) confirms that discriminative signal resides in feature design, not classifier architecture.
We formalize recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification and find that a lightweight pipeline suffices: compute 19 reference-model statistical features (effective dimensionality ${\approx}$4--5 due to multicollinearity; \S\ref{sec:atlas:features}) and classify with a Random Forest into $K{+}1$ depth classes.
To characterize how recursive generation reshapes these features, we construct the \emph{Depth Degradation Atlas}: a $3 \times 3$ grid of model families $\times$ decoding strategies spanning 4 depths (180K samples).
The atlas reveals strategy-dependent degradation trajectories and we introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric to quantify how far into the recursion chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.68\textwidth]{figures/fig_problem_illustration.pdf}
\caption{Recursive generation depth estimation. A seed corpus $\mathcal{D}_0$ feeds a LoRA finetuning--sampling loop producing successively deeper corpora. Given a passage~$x$, the task is to estimate its ordinal depth~$d$.}
\label{fig:problem}
\end{figure*}
Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Task formalization and metric.} We define recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification, introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric, and construct a 180K-sample benchmark ($3$ model families $\times$ $3$ decoding strategies $\times$ $4$ depths).

    \item \textbf{Depth Degradation Atlas.} The perplexity tail feature family and surprisal variance jointly dominate depth discrimination across all 9 cells; $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ in 8/9 cells (4 under nucleus depth extension), validated by 5-class extension (71--80\%); feature group ablation confirms perplexity tail dominance (76.6\% alone vs.\ 78.4\% full set).

    \item \textbf{Systematic characterization.} Cross-model transfer 66.4\% (d1--d3: 55.4\%), cross-domain arXiv 74.1\%, 14B cross-reference 44.1\% ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$); 25--50\% accumulation preserves $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ in 5/6 cells despite $-$8--15\,pp accuracy attenuation. We identify cross-strategy transfer (d1--d3: 45.9\%) as a boundary condition.
\end{itemize}

1	\section{Generalization and Robustness}
2	\label{sec:generalization}
3	
4	We test whether atlas accuracy (68.9--85.9\% four-class; d1--d3: 58.9--81.5\%) reflects genuine statistical regularities across eight generalization axes (five below, three in Appendix).
5	
6	\subsection{Classifier Comparison and Surface-Text Ablation}
7	\label{sec:gen:baselines}
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:baselines} compares methods across all 9 cells.
10	Four classifiers (RF, XGBoost, ordinal MLP, prototypical) converge within 0.8\,pp under cross-model transfer (Appendix~\ref{app:learned_estimator}), confirming a feature-determined accuracy ceiling.
11	
12	\paragraph{Neural end-to-end baselines.}
13	DeBERTa-v3-base (LoRA) underperforms RF by 16--32\,pp (d2 recall 8.4\%); RoBERTa-DCOL (ordinal contrastive; 64.5\%) narrows the gap but remains 14\,pp below RF.
14	
15	\paragraph{Binary detectors and membership inference.}
16	Perturbation-based (DetectGPT, 28.8\%) and membership-inference (Min-K\% Prob, 33.2\%; Min-K\%++ \cite{zhang2024_minkpp} comparable) methods produce scores with no ordinal resolution (Table~\ref{tab:baselines}); CORAL calibration does not close the gap (d1--d3: 40.4\% vs.\ RF 71.6\%).
17	Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024}, calibrated with 11-feature RF, independently converges to 78.1\% ($p{>}0.05$ vs.\ our 78.4\%); merging all 30 features yields 82.6\% (Appendix~\ref{app:feature_ablation_bino}).
18	
19	\paragraph{Surface-text ablation.}
20	Single-feature regression on mean perplexity performs at chance (25.1\%); zero-shot LLMs (best 36.2\%; Appendix~\ref{app:zeroshot_prompt}) also fail; depth signal resides in distributional statistics inaccessible from surface text.
21	
22	\begin{table}[t]
23	\centering
24	\small
25	\caption{Method comparison (RF mean across 9 cells, 5-fold CV). Chance = 25\% / 33.3\% (d1--d3). $^\dagger$Adapted from binary detection; Binoculars 11-feat: $p{>}0.05$ vs.\ 19-feat RF (paired permutation test).}
26	\label{tab:baselines}
27	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
28	\begin{tabular}{@{}llcc@{}}
29	\toprule
30	Method & Calibration & 4-Cl (\%) & d1--d3 (\%) \\
31	\midrule
32	RF 19-feature (ours) & RF & 78.4 & \textbf{71.6} \\
33	Binoculars$^\dagger$ \cite{binoculars2024} & RF (11 feat) & 78.1 & --- \\
34	Merged (30 feat)$^\dagger$ & RF & \textbf{82.6} & --- \\
35	Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024} & threshold & 69.8 & --- \\
36	Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024} & RF (1 feat) & 63.7 & --- \\
37	RoBERTa-DCOL (ordinal) & contrastive & 64.5 & --- \\
38	DeBERTa-v3 (end-to-end) & cross-entropy & 53.1--60.6 & --- \\
39	\midrule
40	Zero-shot LLM (best) & --- & 36.2 & --- \\
41	Min-K\% Prob \cite{shi2024_minkprob} & CORAL & 33.2 & 40.4 \\
42	DetectGPT \cite{mitchell2023_detectgpt} & best-of-3 & 28.8 & 24.3 \\
43	Random & --- & 25.0 & 33.3 \\
44	\bottomrule
45	\end{tabular}}
46	\end{table}
47	
48	\subsection{Cross-Model Transfer}
49	\label{sec:gen:crossmodel}
50	
51	\begin{table}[t]
52	\centering
53	\small
54	\caption{Cross-model transfer (leave-one-out, nucleus only). Chance = 25\% / 33\% (d1--d3). d1--d3 mean 55.4\%; QWK\,=\,0.81; 94.8\% errors at $|\Delta| \leq 1$.}
55	\label{tab:cross_model}
56	\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
57	\toprule
58	Holdout & Acc & d0 & d1 & d2 & d3 \\
59	 & (\%) & Rec. & Rec. & Rec. & Rec. \\
60	\midrule
61	Pythia & 62.4 & 100.0 & 49.3 & 26.8 & 73.6 \\
62	OLMo & \textbf{69.2} & 99.3 & 75.5 & 43.3 & 58.8 \\
63	GPT-2 XL & 67.6 & 98.5 & 74.7 & 52.6 & 44.5 \\
64	\midrule
65	Mean & 66.4 & 99.3 & 66.5 & 40.9 & 59.0 \\
66	\bottomrule
67	\end{tabular}
68	\end{table}
69	
70	Mean transfer accuracy is 66.4\% (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}; d1--d3: 55.4\%, $2.7{\times}$ chance); d2 worst case 26.8\% (Pythia holdout; confusion matrices in Figure~\ref{fig:confusion_matrix}).
71	
72	\subsection{Cross-Strategy Transfer}
73	\label{sec:gen:crossstrategy}
74	
75	Cross-strategy transfer reveals a structural barrier: d1--d3 balanced accuracy drops to 45.9\% (four-class: 59.1\%), 7\,pp below cross-model transfer (Table~\ref{tab:cross_strategy}).
76	A two-stage pipeline (strategy classifier $\to$ conditioned depth classifier) recovers much of this gap: 70.5\% four-class accuracy ($+$11.5\,pp over LOO); oracle routing yields 78.3\%, so the 7.8\,pp residual is attributable to strategy misidentification (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}).
77	Our depth estimation claims hold most strongly within-strategy or when the decoding configuration is known.
78	
79	%% ----------------------------------------------------------------
80	\subsection{Preliminary Cross-Scale Observations (14B)}
81	\label{sec:gen:crossscale}
82	
83	At 14B (Qwen2.5-14B), self-reference yields 50.8\% ($2{\times}$ chance, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$); cross-reference control (Pythia-1.4B) drops accuracy to 44.1\% ($-$6.8\,pp) but raises $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}$ to 2 for nucleus and temperature, revealing that ${\sim}$7\,pp of the accuracy drop is attributable to reference-model mismatch rather than scale (Appendix~\ref{app:cross_scale_full}).
84	Cross-domain (arXiv) accuracy reaches 74.1\% at 1--1.5B; cross-domain FPR is discussed in Limitations.

To test whether detection scores carry complementary ordinal signal, we add Min-K\% probability ($K{=}20$) and DetectGPT perturbation discrepancy as additional RF features.
The 20-feature model (19 + Min-K\%) achieves 78.90\% mean 4-class accuracy (+0.48\,pp) and 72.20\% d1--d3 balanced accuracy (+0.60\,pp).
Min-K\% ranks \#3 by feature importance (0.095), behind \texttt{p90\_ppl} (0.161) and \texttt{var\_surprisal} (0.126); DetectGPT ranks \#17 (0.026).
The marginal improvement is consistent across 8 of 9 atlas cells, indicating that Min-K\%'s token-level log-probability signal provides weak but real complementary information to the passage-level distributional features.
The top-2 features (\texttt{p90\_ppl} + \texttt{var\_surprisal}) retain combined importance of 28.7\%, confirming that perplexity tail statistics remain the dominant depth markers even after augmentation.

\paragraph{Pairwise AUC and ordinal collapse.}
Table~\ref{tab:detector_pairwise_auc} reports pairwise binary AUC for three nucleus cells, contrasting our 19-feature RF with LR-calibrated detector scores and their combination.
Detectors achieve reasonable d0-vs-d1 separation (Combined AUC\,$\geq$\,0.949), but d1-vs-d2 and d2-vs-d3 AUC collapse toward chance (0.50--0.77), far below the RF pipeline (0.930--0.958 and 0.813--0.892 respectively).
This confirms that binary detection scores capture the real-vs-synthetic boundary but lack the ordinal gradient needed to distinguish recursive depths.

1031	The 13.8\,pp drop relative to BOS-seeded generation is expected: topic prompts constrain the output distribution, reducing the variance that distinguishes depths.
1032	Nevertheless, accuracy remains $2.8\times$ chance and pairwise AUC decays monotonically (0.916, 0.782, 0.744); the depth signal is therefore not an artifact of unconstrained generation.
1033	Top features are identical to BOS-seeded (\texttt{p90\_ppl} first); the same perplexity tail erosion mechanism operates under prompted conditions.
1034	
1035	\subsection{Extended Discussion}
1036	\label{app:extended_discussion}
1037	
1038	\paragraph{Cross-strategy conditional decomposition.}
1039	The two-stage pipeline (strategy identification followed by depth classification) recovers 11.5\,pp over the na\"ive pooled classifier.
1040	Under correct strategy routing, four-class accuracy reaches 72.6\% vs.\ 68.0\% under misrouting ($N{=}103{,}498$ / $76{,}502$), a gap of 4.6\,pp; d0 accuracy remains near-ceiling (${\sim}99.6$\%) regardless of routing, confirming that the d0 signal is strategy-invariant.
1041	Even the worst routing yields a floor of 67.6\% ($2.7\times$ chance), and the 31.5\,pp d1--d3 gap between correct and wrong routing confirms feature-space misalignment rather than uniform noise.
1042	End-to-end PLMs lag RF by ${\sim}20$\,pp, suggesting that current pretrained representations do not capture the distributional tail statistics that drive depth discrimination.
1043	
1044	\paragraph{Depth-graduated curation (inconclusive).}
1045	Initial curation experiments remain inconclusive: RF-vs-unfiltered is not significant ($p>0.4$; Appendix~\ref{app:curation_poc}).
1046	
1047	\paragraph{Toward a provenance toolkit.}
1048	Depth estimation complements existing provenance methods along orthogonal axes.
1049	Watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} provides high-confidence attribution when the generator cooperates but is inapplicable to unwatermarked text.
1050	Source attribution \cite{uchendu2020_attribution} identifies the generating model but not the generation history.
1051	Depth estimation characterizes \emph{iterative reuse} regardless of generator cooperation or identity.
1052	A layered provenance system combining these three signals (watermark presence, source model, and recursive generation depth) could support more nuanced data auditing than any single method.
1053	
1054	\subsection{Computational Resources and Reproducibility}
1055	\label{app:compute}
1056	
1057	\paragraph{Hardware.}
1058	All experiments were conducted on 2$\times$ NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (48\,GB) GPUs locally and 2$\times$ NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (48\,GB) on cloud instances.
1059	Total computation is approximately 200 GPU$\cdot$hours, covering the $3 \times 3$ generation matrix (LoRA fine-tuning + sampling at each depth), feature extraction, depth extension to d5, 7--14B QLoRA experiments, and all ablations.

Key observations from the updated paper:

1. **Discussion expanded** ✅ — Now has "Multi-channel depth encoding" + "Deployment considerations" paragraphs. Much better than the 3-sentence version.

Let me check if those reversal values (0.13/0.25) appear anywhere in the main text. The cross-strategy reversal is discussed qualitatively, but I need to verify whether the actual AUC numbers are present.

5. **Detector baselines pairwise AUC** — The appendix has a table showing detector methods like Binoculars and Fast-DetectGPT collapse toward 0.50 AUC while RF stays above 0.930, which is compelling evidence but currently only in the appendix.

Now I'm assessing what this means for the EMNLP review.

The paper would likely receive scores around 3-3.5 across soundness, novelty, and significance. The core issue is that while the task formalization and systematic empirical study are legitimate contributions, the lack of algorithmic novelty is the biggest vulnerability — reviewers looking for methodological innovation will see this as just applying standard random forests to hand-crafted features. The 4-classifier convergence argument is clever in showing the signal lives in the features rather than the model, but that's a subtle point that might not overcome the novelty concern. Beyond that, the scale limitations of the study create questions about how well findings generalize beyond the specific experimental setup.

The practical utility of the approach breaks down at larger model scales — 14B accuracy barely exceeds chance at 44-50%, which the paper frames honestly as signal attenuation but leaves the method largely unusable for modern LLMs. The cross-strategy transfer failure is even more damaging: the two-stage pipeline recovers to 70.5% accuracy, but only when the strategy is known in advance. In realistic scenarios where you'd need to identify the strategy first, the strategy classifier itself only reaches 57.8%, making the whole pipeline unreliable. The paper does acknowledge this by presenting oracle routing results showing what's theoretically possible, but that gap between oracle and practical performance is a major limitation. The accumulation results showing 5 out of 6 cells preserve the EDD=3 property substantially address this concern. The reference model dependency remains a practical limitation though — it requires a fixed reference and shows a 4-11pp self-reference advantage without a principled selection criterion, which constrains real-world deployment.

On the minor side, the d0 recall inflation above 97% does inflate the headline 4-class numbers, though the paper mitigates this by reporting d1-d3 separately. There's also uncertainty from using a single LoRA seed (roughly 1-3pp), with seed replication in the appendix but not quantified in the main text. The results are primarily Wikipedia-based; the arXiv cross-domain evaluation at 74.1% shows some transfer capability but indicates limited coverage beyond that domain. Per-strategy d1v2 analysis is incomplete.

The UC reversal values should appear in the Discussion section per D015 but only the qualitative description made it in. More critically, the detector baselines pairwise AUC results showing ordinal collapse are powerful evidence — Binoculars and DetectGPT collapse to ~0.50 AUC while the random forest maintains 0.93 — this directly demonstrates why binary detectors can't perform depth estimation, yet it's relegated to the appendix when it deserves main text prominence.

For the M1 weakness about lacking a novel method, I can't fundamentally fix that, but I can reposition the contribution by adding context in the Introduction about precedent papers like HELM, MMLU, and MAGE that are benchmark and analysis focused, and by promoting the ordinal collapse finding to the main text since it strengthens the task formalization angle. The M2 scale limitation could potentially be addressed by running additional experiments with the available GPU resources. one more 7-8B experiment with matched reference model (7B model as reference for 7B generator). This would test whether scale attenuation is partly reference mismatch.
- But 3 days with 1 GPU: LoRA fine-tune + generate for 3 depths + feature extraction = ~12-18 GPU-hours. Feasible but tight.
- Alternative: just tighten the narrative. The paper already positions 14B as "preliminary observations."

**For M3 (Cross-strategy):**
- The two-stage pipeline is now in main text. The oracle gap (7.8pp from misrouting) is clearly stated.
- Could add the per-strategy d1v2 AUC table to main text or Discussion per D015.
- No experiment can fix this in 3 days — it's a fundamental structural barrier.

**For M4 (Full-replacement):**
- Already well-mitigated with 6 accumulation cells. Could run 1-2 more accumulation cells testing different strategies like temp/topk under accumulation to strengthen the findings — each would take about 4 GPU-hours and is doable.

**For M5 (Reference model):**
- Already acknowledged in Limitations. No easy fix in 3 days.

### Plan_018 ordinal collapse:

The pairwise AUC table showing Binoculars d1v2 AUC at 0.50-0.53 versus RF at 0.93-0.96 is the key evidence for ordinal collapse — detectors can distinguish real from synthetic but fail to capture depth gradients. Moving this from the appendix to the main text, perhaps by adding a row to Table 4 showing d1v2 AUC alongside 4-class accuracy, would make this argument much more prominent.

The experiment coverage is fairly comprehensive for an EMNLP detection paper: multiple models, strategies, and baselines are all covered, plus cross-model transfer, cross-domain evaluation, feature ablation, scale extension to 14B, and accumulation scenarios. The main gaps are adversarial robustness (paraphrase attacks) and multi-lingual evaluation, both noted in Limitations, plus only 3 model families tested — though a fourth 7-8B experiment with matched reference model could test whether scale attenuation is partly reference mismatch, but that's tight on the 3-day timeline with 1 GPU.

The Limitations section is solid with three well-quantified paragraphs covering full-replacement vs accumulation, scale and cross-strategy effects, and reference model dependency. However, there's a hard constraint (D015) requiring explicit mention of the cross-strategy deployment constraint in Limitations — specifically that deploying across strategies requires prior knowledge of the target strategy, which isn't always available in practice. This needs to be stated clearly rather than buried in the appendix.

The 14B scale narrative is appropriately cautious, with the Abstract noting signal attenuation (~44% cross-reference accuracy at 14B), Section 5.4 hedged as "preliminary observations," and the theory predicting this attenuation from the scaling exponent. The framing is reasonable but I should verify the constraint is fully satisfied.

A reviewer will likely push back on the 14B results, arguing the method doesn't scale. My defense relies on three points: reference mismatch explains ~7 percentage points of the gap, signal still exists at 14B (EDD=2 for nucleus/temperature), and scale-matched references could recover performance. The weak spot is that I haven't tested scale-matched references—a valid critique that's hard to address without a 14B reference model and significant compute. I'll compile the full review now.

\subsection{Temperature Robustness}
\label{app:multi_tau}

The cross-strategy results in \S\ref{sec:gen:crossstrategy} use a single temperature ($\tau{=}0.9$).
To test whether depth signal generalizes across temperatures, we repeat the classification pipeline at $\tau \in \{0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1\}$ on Pythia-1.4B.

\paragraph{Within-$\tau$ robustness.}
For $\tau \in [0.5, 0.9]$, d1-vs-d2 AUC exceeds 0.80 (peak 0.851 at $\tau{=}0.7$, comparable to nucleus $p{=}0.95$'s 0.861) and 4-class accuracy ranges from 75.4\% to 77.3\% (Table~\ref{tab:multi_tau_within}); the depth signal is therefore not an artifact of a single temperature.
The same top-5 features (\texttt{var\_surprisal}, \texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{mean\_ppl}, \texttt{mean\_surprisal}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}) dominate across all $\tau$ values with only minor rank-order variation.

\paragraph{Collapse at $\tau{=}1.1$: memorization as prerequisite.}
At $\tau{=}1.1$, 4-class accuracy drops to 57.2\% and d1v2 AUC falls to 0.528.
Training loss reveals the mechanism: at low temperature ($\tau{=}0.5$), fine-tuning loss decreases steeply across recursive depths ($2.27 \to 0.42 \to 0.16$), a sign of rapid memorization of the model's own output.
At $\tau{=}1.1$, loss remains nearly flat ($2.27 \to 1.91 \to 1.85$); high-entropy output resists memorization, so depth-dependent distributional shifts do not accumulate.
This establishes \emph{memorization as a prerequisite} for detectable depth signal: recursive depth is discriminable only when successive fine-tuning iterations progressively reshape the output distribution.

\paragraph{Cross-$\tau$ non-transferability.}
Leave-one-$\tau$-out transfer yields mean accuracy of 46.7\% with mean d1v2 AUC of 0.319 (Table~\ref{tab:multi_tau_cross}), worse than cross-strategy transfer (59.1\%; \S\ref{sec:gen:crossstrategy}).
Holdout $\tau{=}0.5$ produces inverted d1v2 AUC (0.176); different temperatures therefore produce surprisal distributions with incompatible shapes.
This extends the strategy-specificity finding: even within a single decoding family, the feature space is temperature-specific; strategy-conditioned classifiers are therefore necessary.

\paragraph{Ecological validity.}

[severity: warning] 完整 EMNLP 2026 ARR 模拟审稿（第二轮，基于最新定稿版本）

---

## 预估评分

| 维度 | 分数 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| Soundness | 3.5/5 | 9-cell atlas 内数据扎实，accumulation/14B 诚实报告 |
| Novelty | 3.0/5 | 任务形式化 + EDD 指标是新的，方法（RF+features）是标准的 |
| Significance | 3.0/5 | 问题重要，但 scale limitation 限制实际影响力 |
| **Overall Assessment** | **3.0–3.5** | **Findings 到 Borderline Conference** |

Best case 3.5（重视 task formalization + New Missions fit 的 reviewer）。Expected 3.0（Findings）。Worst case 2.5（要求 method contribution 的 reviewer）。

---

## MAJOR Weaknesses（按危险程度排序）

### M1. 无算法创新 [风险: HIGH — 最可能导致拒稿]

论文贡献定位为 "task formalization + systematic empirical study"，classifier 是标准 RF。§1 坦诚说 "contribution centers on task formalization...rather than algorithmic novelty"，但 EMNLP 审稿人对 "RF on features" 的接受度因人而异。

**当前防线**：4-classifier 收敛在 0.8pp 内（signal in features, not classifier）；EDD 是新指标；ordinal collapse finding。

**3 天补救（无需 GPU）**：
1. **[强烈建议] 将 ordinal collapse 证据从 appendix 提升到主文**。当前 appendix B.29 Table (tab:detector_pairwise_auc) 显示 Binoculars d1v2 AUC = 0.50–0.53 而 RF = 0.93–0.96——这是论文最强的 "depth estimation ≠ binary detection" 证据。可在 §5.1 Table 4 增加一列 "d1v2 AUC" 或在正文补一句 "Detector scores collapse to chance-level ordinal resolution: Binoculars d1v2 AUC 0.51 vs RF 0.93 (Appendix B.29)"。这强化了 task formalization 的独立贡献。
2. Introduction 中引用 HELM/MMLU/MAGE 作为 benchmark/analysis paper 先例（1 句话）。

### M2. 尺度泛化弱 [风险: HIGH]

14B cross-ref: 44.1%（4 类 chance=25%, 仅 1.76× chance）。现代 LLM 主流 70B+，1–1.5B 结果的实际部署价值有限。

**当前防线**：§5.4 标题 "Preliminary Cross-Scale Observations"（审慎措辞）；reference mismatch 占 ~7pp；theory 预测 scale attenuation。

**3 天补救（需 GPU，可选）**：
- **方案 A（推荐，~15 GPU-hours）**：用 Qwen2.5-7B FP16 跑一组 clean 实验（3 depths × nucleus），用 7B 模型自身做 reference model。这直接测试 "scale-matched reference 能否恢复信号"。如果 7B self-ref accuracy ≥60%，可大幅强化 "scale attenuation is partly reference mismatch" 的论点。当前 7-8B 附录结果因 QLoRA confounds 不可靠。
- **方案 B（纯编辑）**：不跑新实验，但在 Discussion 明确写 "Scale-matched reference models (same architecture and scale as the generator) represent the most promising direction for recovering depth signal at larger scales; our 14B results with a mismatched 1.4B reference model likely underestimate the true discriminability."

### M3. 跨策略失败 [风险: MEDIUM-HIGH]

d1–d3: 45.9%，仅略高于 33% chance。两阶段 pipeline 恢复到 70.5%（+11.5pp），但策略分类器仅 57.8%。温度采样 d1v2 AUC 低至 0.13（GPT-2 XL）和 0.25（OLMo）——预测字面反转。

**当前防线**：§5.3 现在有完整数字；Abstract 诚实说 "claims hold most strongly within-strategy"；Limitations 提到 cross-strategy transfer。

**3 天补救（无需 GPU）**：
- **[D015 硬约束未完全满足]** Discussion 需包含 per-strategy d1v2 AUC 值。当前 Discussion 定性提到策略效应但未报告 0.13/0.25 这些关键反转值。建议在 Discussion "Deployment considerations" 段补一句："Cross-strategy d1v2 AUC can invert to as low as 0.13 when temperature-sampled text is classified by a nucleus-trained model, underscoring the requirement for strategy-aware deployment."
- **Limitations 段 2 补充**（D015 要求）：明确写 "Cross-strategy deployment requires a priori knowledge of the target decoding strategy; without it, d1/d2 predictions may invert."

### M4. Full-replacement vs 现实 [风险: MEDIUM]

现实世界是 accumulation，论文用 full-replacement。

**当前防线强**：6 个 accumulation cells（3 models × 2 mix ratios），5/6 保持 EDD=3，边界 case（GPT-2 XL mix50 d2v3=0.695）诚实报告。这个弱点已被充分缓解。

**3 天补救（可选，~8 GPU-hours）**：
- 跑 1-2 个 temp/topk 策略下的 accumulation cell，扩展当前仅 nucleus 的 accumulation 覆盖。但优先级低于 M2。

### M5. d2 recall 低 [风险: MEDIUM-LOW]

d2 in-distribution recall 44–73%，cross-model worst case 26.8%（Pythia holdout）。

**当前防线**：理论解释（depth gradient 中心）；QWK=0.81；94.8% errors ≤1；d2 是 EDD bottleneck 的理论预测。已充分防御。

---

## MINOR Weaknesses

| # | 问题 | 影响 |
|---|------|------|
| m1 | 单一 LoRA seed (~1-3pp uncertainty) | LOW — 附录有 seed replication |
| m2 | Wikipedia-centric 主基准 | LOW — arXiv 跨域 74.1% 已有 |
| m3 | 无对抗鲁棒性（paraphrase attacks） | LOW — Limitations 提及 |
| m4 | D015 d1v2 反转值未进主文 | MEDIUM — 编辑即可修复 |
| m5 | Ordinal collapse 证据仅在 appendix | MEDIUM — 提升到主文可显著提分 |
| m6 | 31 orphan labels（2 个 display items） | LOW — fig:confusion_matrix 已修复，tab:downstream 待修 |

---

## 专项评估

### plan_018 ordinal collapse 对 claim 强度的提升

**有显著提升空间。** Appendix B.29 Table (tab:detector_pairwise_auc) 是论文被低估的最强证据之一：

| Method | d0v1 AUC | d1v2 AUC | d2v3 AUC |
|--------|----------|----------|----------|
| RF-19feat | 0.997–0.999 | **0.930–0.958** | **0.813–0.892** |
| Binoculars | 0.738–0.942 | **0.502–0.529** | 0.515–0.581 |
| Combined | 0.949–0.990 | 0.724–0.767 | 0.550–0.703 |

Binoculars 在 d1v2 几乎是 random（0.50）——这直接证明 binary detection scores 没有 ordinal resolution。当前仅在 appendix，但这个 finding 应该在 §5.1 的 Table 4 附近展示。

**建议**：在 Table 4 caption 或正文补充 "Pairwise AUC analysis confirms ordinal collapse: detector d1v2 AUC collapses to 0.50–0.53 vs RF 0.93 (Appendix B.29)"。

### 实验覆盖空缺评估

对比同领域顶会（MAGE/Binoculars/Ghostbuster/RAID）的标准：

| 维度 | 状态 | 评估 |
|------|------|------|
| 多模型（≥3） | ✅ 3 families | 充分 |
| 多策略 | ✅ 3 strategies | 充分 |
| Baselines（≥4） | ✅ 8+ methods | 超过平均水平 |
| Cross-model transfer | ✅ LOO | 充分 |
| Cross-domain | ✅ arXiv + WikiText + C4 | 充分 |
| Feature ablation | ✅ 4 levels + group + Binoculars | 超过平均水平 |
| Scale extension | ✅ 14B + 7-8B | 有但结果弱 |
| Accumulation | ✅ 6 cells | 良好 |
| Error bars/CI | ✅ Bootstrap CI | 充分 |
| Adversarial robustness | ❌ 未测试 | 可接受（Limitations 提及） |
| Statistical tests | ⚠️ 部分有 | 可改进（多重比较未校正，已注明 footnote） |

**结论：实验覆盖在同类论文中处于上游水平。** 无明显空缺会被 reviewer 作为 rejection 理由。

### Limitations 充分性

| 弱点 | Limitations 是否覆盖 | 评估 |
|------|---------------------|------|
| Full-replacement | ✅ 第 1 段，量化 | 充分 |
| Scale attenuation | ✅ 第 2 段 | 充分 |
| Reference model | ✅ 第 3 段 | 充分 |
| Cross-strategy reversal | ⚠️ 第 2 段提到 45.9% 但未写 d1/d2 反转风险 | **D015 未满足** |
| Single seed | ✅ 第 3 段 "additional caveats" | 充分 |
| Length sensitivity | ✅ 附录 | 充分 |
| FPR on wild data | ✅ 第 2 段 | 充分 |

**缺口**：Limitations 第 2 段需补充 "Cross-strategy deployment requires prior knowledge of decoding strategy; without it, d1/d2 predictions may invert"（D015 硬约束）。

### 14B 叙事攻击风险

**风险等级：MEDIUM。** 当前叙事策略合理：
- §5.4 标题 "Preliminary Cross-Scale Observations" ✓
- Reference mismatch 占 ~7pp 的解构 ✓
- Theory 预测一致（α closer to 1 → weaker signal） ✓

**主要攻击角度**：
1. "Method barely works at 14B, so it's useless for real deployment" → 防御：14B 证明信号存在（EDD=2），reference mismatch 是 recoverable 的
2. "Why not test with 14B reference model?" → 目前无防御（compute 限制）。建议在 Discussion 补一句预测方向。
3. "7-8B results are contradictory — what does that mean?" → 已在 appendix 解释为 QLoRA confounds

**最大风险**：如果审稿人认为 "14B 不 work = method 没用"，这是 hard reject territory。但 "New Missions" track 审稿人更可能接受 "controlled study at 1-1.5B + preliminary scale evidence" 的框架。

---

## 3 天行动优先级（1 GPU available）

| 优先级 | 行动 | 类型 | 预计耗时 | 预期提分 |
|--------|------|------|----------|----------|
| P0 | D015：Limitations + Discussion 补 cross-strategy d1v2 反转具体数值 | 编辑 | 30min | +0.1 (消除硬约束违规) |

| P1 | Qwen2.5-7B FP16 clean 实验 (self-ref, nucleus, 3 depths) | GPU | ~15h | +0.2 if successful (缓解 M2) |
| P2 | tab:downstream orphan label 修复 + caption B 值统一 | 编辑 | 15min | +0.05 |
| P3 | Accumulation 扩展到 temp/topk (1-2 cells) | GPU | ~8h | +0.05 |

1	\section{Related Work}
2	\label{sec:related}
3	
4	\paragraph{Model Collapse Theory.}
5	Recursive training on model outputs erodes distributional tails \cite{shumailov2024_nature}, an effect formalized as exponential tail decay via scaling laws \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails,seddik2024synthetic} and extended to autophagous loops in the MAD framework \cite{alemohammad2024_mad} and Markovian generation chains \cite{geng2026_markovian}.
6	Subsequent work refines the conditions under which collapse occurs: \citet{bertrand2024_stability} identify convergence to a fixed point under mixed real-synthetic retraining (providing theoretical grounding for our EDD ceiling, \S\ref{sec:method:theory}), \citet{shi2025_closer_look} reframe collapse as a generalization-to-memorization transition, and \citet{dohmatob2025_strong_collapse} extend guarantees to broader model classes.
7	Mitigation \cite{gerstgrasser2024_accumulate,drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse,yi2026_escaping_collapse,falahati2026_curated,wenzek2020_ccnet}, data scaling under constraint \cite{muennighoff2023scaling}, non-monotonic dynamics \cite{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement}, convergence analysis \cite{marchi2024_heat_death,wang2026_contamination,knowledge_collapse2025,dohmatob2024_demystified}, and diversity decline \cite{guo2024curious,briesch2024selfconsuming,padmakumar2024diversity,sigma2026_spectral,synthetic_eggs2026} are active areas.
8	\citet{kazdan2025_collapse_or_thrive} systematically compare training workflows and show that data accumulation avoids collapse while pure replacement does not; \citet{suresh2025_rate_collapse} characterize the rate of collapse for fundamental distributions under recursive maximum-likelihood estimation.
9	\citet{schaeffer2025} argue that ``model collapse'' conflates multiple phenomena and call for operationally precise metrics; we respond by operationalizing tail-erosion predictions into a deployable ordinal classifier that reveals strategy-dependent trajectories and non-monotonic 7B behavior that the theory does not predict.
10	All assume depth is known a priori; we address the inverse problem of estimating depth from text alone.
11	
12	\paragraph{AI Text Detection.}

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Model Collapse Theory.}
Recursive training on model outputs erodes distributional tails \cite{shumailov2024_nature}, an effect formalized as exponential tail decay via scaling laws \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails,seddik2024synthetic} and extended to autophagous loops in the MAD framework \cite{alemohammad2024_mad} and Markovian generation chains \cite{geng2026_markovian}.
Subsequent work refines the conditions under which collapse occurs: \citet{bertrand2024_stability} identify convergence to a fixed point under mixed real-synthetic retraining (providing theoretical grounding for our EDD ceiling, \S\ref{sec:method:theory}), \citet{shi2025_closer_look} reframe collapse as a generalization-to-memorization transition, and \citet{dohmatob2025_strong_collapse} extend guarantees to broader model classes.
Mitigation \cite{gerstgrasser2024_accumulate,drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse,yi2026_escaping_collapse,falahati2026_curated,wenzek2020_ccnet}, data scaling under constraint \cite{muennighoff2023scaling}, non-monotonic dynamics \cite{bakshi2026_collapse_improvement}, convergence analysis \cite{marchi2024_heat_death,wang2026_contamination,knowledge_collapse2025,dohmatob2024_demystified}, and diversity decline \cite{guo2024curious,briesch2024selfconsuming,padmakumar2024diversity,sigma2026_spectral,synthetic_eggs2026} are active areas.
\citet{kazdan2025_collapse_or_thrive} systematically compare training workflows and show that data accumulation avoids collapse while pure replacement does not; \citet{suresh2025_rate_collapse} characterize the rate of collapse for fundamental distributions under recursive maximum-likelihood estimation.
\citet{schaeffer2025} argue that ``model collapse'' conflates multiple phenomena and call for operationally precise metrics; we respond by operationalizing tail-erosion predictions into a deployable ordinal classifier that reveals strategy-dependent trajectories and non-monotonic 7B behavior that the theory does not predict.
All assume depth is known a priori; we address the inverse problem of estimating depth from text alone.

\paragraph{AI Text Detection.}
The detection literature \cite{wu2025_detection_survey} spans statistical methods (DetectGPT \cite{mitchell2023_detectgpt}, Fast-DetectGPT \cite{fast_detectgpt2024}, Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024}, DivEye \cite{diveye2026}, BiScope \cite{guo2024_biscope}, GLTR \cite{gehrmann2019_gltr}, Ghostbuster \cite{verma2024_ghostbuster}, DNA-GPT \cite{yang2024_dnagpt}), geometric approaches based on intrinsic dimensionality \cite{tulchinskii2023_intrinsic_dim}, and watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark}, with known limits from paraphrasing \cite{sadasivan2023_paraphrase}, distribution shift \cite{pudasaini2026_detection_fails}, and generator barriers \cite{pu2026_generator_barrier}.
\citet{wang2023_seqxgpt} address sentence-level attribution by using log-probability features from white-box LLMs.
M4-SemEval \cite{wang2024_m4_semeval}, MAGE \cite{li2024_mage}, and the PAN 2026 shared tasks \cite{bevendorff2026_pan} benchmark detection across domains, models, and adversarial conditions; RAID \cite{dugan2024_raid} targets binary detection across diverse attack vectors rather than ordinal depth estimation, making direct protocol adoption inapplicable to our task.
\citet{bevendorff2025_two_paradigms} distinguish authorship attribution (which model?) from verification (human or AI?); depth estimation introduces a third axis: which recursive iteration.
All these methods perform binary classification, discarding ordinal depth information; our approach outputs ordinal depth labels, complementing rather than replacing binary detection.

\paragraph{Membership Inference and Data Provenance.}
\citet{carlini2021_extracting} demonstrate that training data can be extracted from LLMs, motivating provenance-aware pipelines.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

The text on which large language models are trained increasingly contains their own outputs.
As synthetic content proliferates across the web, a recursive loop emerges: models trained on web corpora ingest text generated by earlier models, and their outputs feed into the next generation's training data \cite{shumailov2024_nature,alemohammad2024_mad}.
This model$\to$data$\to$model cycle is no longer hypothetical; it is already occurring in the wild. Yet whether the recursive generation depth of a text can be estimated from its statistical properties remains unstudied, a question that matters because first-generation synthetic text may be benign or even beneficial for training, while deeply recursive text drives the distributional collapse that degrades model quality \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}.
In this work, we focus on the 1--1.5B parameter regime under \emph{controlled full-replacement chains}, where each generation fully replaces the prior training set, isolating the depth variable. Real-world contamination typically involves partial mixing (accumulation), where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions; the full-replacement setting provides an upper bound on depth signal strength, and we discuss implications for accumulation settings in \S\ref{sec:discussion}.

Existing tools address adjacent but distinct problems.
Binary detectors \cite{binoculars2024,fast_detectgpt2024,diveye2026} collapse all depths $d \geq 1$ into a single category; watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} requires proactive embedding.
The model collapse literature \cite{shumailov2024_nature,dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails} assumes depth is known a priori; \citet{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse} filter synthetic data via binary detection without distinguishing depths.
No existing method estimates the ordinal recursive generation depth of a text passage from its content alone (Figure~\ref{fig:problem}).

We find that recursive generation leaves quantifiable statistical fingerprints in text, and these fingerprints are \textbf{consistent in direction but scale-dependent in magnitude} across the three model families and three decoding strategies studied.
Specifically, the perplexity tail feature family (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) and surprisal variance emerge as dominant depth indicators, with group-level dominance robust across all 9 model--strategy configurations and three importance measures.
Following the tradition of benchmark-driven empirical studies in NLP, our contribution centers on task formalization and systematic empirical characterization rather than algorithmic novelty; the convergence of four classifiers within 0.8\,pp (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}) confirms that discriminative signal resides in feature design, not classifier architecture.
We formalize recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification and find that a lightweight pipeline suffices: compute 19 reference-model statistical features (effective dimensionality ${\approx}$4--5 due to multicollinearity; \S\ref{sec:atlas:features}) and classify with a Random Forest into $K{+}1$ depth classes.
To characterize how recursive generation reshapes these features, we construct the \emph{Depth Degradation Atlas}: a $3 \times 3$ grid of model families $\times$ decoding strategies spanning 4 depths (180K samples).
The atlas reveals strategy-dependent degradation trajectories and we introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric to quantify how far into the recursion chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.68\textwidth]{figures/fig_problem_illustration.pdf}
\caption{Recursive generation depth estimation. A seed corpus $\mathcal{D}_0$ feeds a LoRA finetuning--sampling loop producing successively deeper corpora. Given a passage~$x$, the task is to estimate its ordinal depth~$d$.}
\label{fig:problem}
\end{figure*}
Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Task formalization and metric.} We define recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification, introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric, and construct a 180K-sample benchmark ($3$ model families $\times$ $3$ decoding strategies $\times$ $4$ depths).

    \item \textbf{Depth Degradation Atlas.} The perplexity tail feature family and surprisal variance jointly dominate depth discrimination across all 9 cells; $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ in 8/9 cells (4 under nucleus depth extension), validated by 5-class extension (71--80\%); feature group ablation confirms perplexity tail dominance (76.6\% alone vs.\ 78.4\% full set).

    \item \textbf{Systematic characterization.} Cross-model transfer 66.4\% (d1--d3: 55.4\%), cross-domain arXiv 74.1\%, 14B cross-reference 44.1\% ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$); 25--50\% accumulation preserves $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ in 5/6 cells despite $-$8--15\,pp accuracy attenuation. We identify cross-strategy transfer (d1--d3: 45.9\%) as a boundary condition.
\end{itemize}

[severity: info] Novelty 写作强化四角度逐项评估

基于当前定稿版本（已确认 §5.1:16 已含 ordinal collapse 数字）。

---

## 角度 1: EDD 指标独特性

**(a) 值得改？YES，小改，安全。**

当前表述："We propose the Effective Discriminable Depth (EDD) as an operational measure"（method.tex:82）。Introduction:19 说 "we introduce the EDD metric"。都是中性动词，没有强调 "first"。

**(b) 具体改哪里？**

- **Introduction:19** — 当前："we introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric to quantify how far into the recursion chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable"。建议改为："we introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD), to our knowledge the first operational metric for ordinal depth resolution in recursive generation, quantifying how far into the recursion chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable"。

- **method.tex:82** — 可选补一句连接 information theory："EDD operationalizes the intuition that recursive generation contracts mutual information between adjacent depth distributions at a rate that depends on model scale and decoding strategy"。但这需要谨慎——论文没有正式计算 mutual information，所以只能说 "operationalizes the intuition" 而非 "measures mutual information"。

**(c) Overreach 风险？LOW。** EDD 确实是文献中首个此类指标。没有任何 prior work 定义 ordinal depth resolution metric（model collapse 文献假设 depth 已知，detection 文献做 binary）。claim "to our knowledge the first" 有充分支撑。

信息论连接风险 MEDIUM——如果只是 "intuition" 级别的类比可以写，如果暗示 formal information-theoretic analysis 则属 overclaim（论文没算 MI/KL 的 depth 衰减）。

**建议**：只改 Introduction:19 加 "to our knowledge the first"，不加信息论连接（风险 > 收益，且可能引发 reviewer 追问 "why didn't you formally compute MI?"）。

---

## 角度 2: Task formalization 与 binary detection 的理论界限

**(a) 值得改？部分值得。**

当前 Related Work:16-17 已经做了清晰的界限划分："depth estimation introduces a third axis: which recursive iteration"。Introduction:12 也说 "No existing method estimates the ordinal recursive generation depth"。§5.1:16 已含 ordinal collapse 数字（Binoculars d1v2 AUC=0.50-0.53 vs RF 0.93）。

**缺失的是 Introduction 中对 ordinal collapse 的预告。** 当前 Introduction 第二段（lines 9-12）列举了 existing tools 的不足，但只说 "collapse all depths d≥1 into a single category"——这是逻辑论证。如果加上 ordinal collapse 的经验证据预告，会更有力。

**(b) 具体改哪里？**

- **Introduction:10** — 当前："Binary detectors \cite{...} collapse all depths $d \geq 1$ into a single category"。建议在本句后补半句："—a limitation we confirm empirically: their pairwise d1-vs-d2 AUC collapses to chance level (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines})"。

这把 "binary detectors can't do depth" 从逻辑论证升级为经验+逻辑双重论证，且在 Introduction 就预告了 §5.1 的关键发现。

- **Related Work:17** — 当前已经足够好，无需改。"All these methods perform binary classification, discarding ordinal depth information; our approach outputs ordinal depth labels"——清晰且准确。

**(c) Overreach 风险？LOW。** ordinal collapse 是实验事实（d1v2 AUC=0.50），在 Introduction 预告完全合理。只需确保措辞是 "confirm empirically" 而非 "prove"。

---

## 角度 3: Multi-channel depth encoding 的 Abstract/Introduction 可见性

**(a) 值得改？不建议改。**

当前状态已经足够：
- **Abstract:5** 已含 "corroborated by classifier convergence and independent cross-perplexity features"
- **Discussion:4-6** 完整展开了 multi-channel 论点（W=0.90, Binoculars 78.1% vs 78.4% indistinguishable, merged 82.6%）
- **Introduction:15-16** 已含 "convergence of four classifiers within 0.8 pp confirms that discriminative signal resides in feature design"

在 Abstract/Introduction 进一步强调 multi-channel 会有两个问题：
1. **挤占空间**——Abstract 已经 8 句，Introduction 已经很密。增加 multi-channel 强调意味着减少其他内容。
2. **Contribution mismatch**——multi-channel 是 Discussion 级 finding，不是 contribution list 中的条目。如果 Abstract 给它太多篇幅，会让 reviewer 期待一个更深入的 multi-channel analysis，但论文实际只有 Binoculars 一条独立路径验证。

**(c) Overreach 风险？MEDIUM。** "distributional property, not a single exploitable artifact" 这个 claim 的证据是：4 种 importance measures 一致 + 1 条独立路径（Binoculars）收敛。如果在 Abstract 更 prominently 声称 "multi-channel encoding"，审稿人可能追问 "only two independent feature pathways is not strong evidence for 'multiple channels'"。

**建议：维持现状。** Discussion + Abstract 的当前覆盖已足够。不值得为 +0.05 提分冒 overreach 风险。

---

## 角度 4: Ordinal collapse 作为独立 contribution

**(a) 值得改？不建议列为独立 contribution，但可在正文中更 prominently 框架为 "finding"。**

理由：
1. **Ordinal collapse 是 supporting evidence，不是 standalone contribution。** 它的作用是证明 "depth estimation ≠ binary detection"，支撑 Contribution 1（task formalization）。如果列为独立 contribution（第 4 条），审稿人会问 "what's the insight beyond 'binary scores don't have ordinal gradient'? Isn't that obvious by definition?"
2. **Contribution list 已经有 3 条**，符合 EMNLP 惯例（3 条是甜点，4 条开始显得分散）。
3. §5.1:16 已经在主文含了关键数字——它作为 §5.1 的一部分比作为独立 contribution 更自然。

**(b) 如果要强化（不作为 contribution 但增加可见性）：**

- **§5.1 paragraph "Binary detectors and membership inference"**（generalization.tex:15-18）——当前这段有 ordinal collapse 数字但混在一大段里。可以考虑给 ordinal collapse 一个独立的 paragraph 标题：`\paragraph{Ordinal collapse of detection scores.}` 把 line 16 的 "pairwise analysis confirms ordinal collapse" 独立成段。这在视觉上突出 finding 而不改变 contribution 声明。

- 但这有空间成本——8 页已经很满，新增 paragraph 标题会吃掉一行。

**(c) Overreach 风险？如果列为 contribution: HIGH。** "Binary detectors lack ordinal resolution" 接近 tautological（它们设计就是 binary 的）。论文的真正贡献是量化了这个差距（d1v2 0.50 vs 0.93），这作为 supporting evidence 有力，但作为 standalone contribution 太薄。

**建议：维持现状。** §5.1:16 已有关键数字。如果空间允许，可以给它加一个 paragraph 标题增加视觉可见性，但不列入 contribution list。

---

## 总结优先级

| 角度 | 改？ | 改动量 | 预期提分 | Overreach 风险 |
|------|------|--------|----------|---------------|
| 1. EDD "first" | ✅ YES | 5 words (Introduction:19) | +0.1 | LOW |
| 2. Intro 预告 ordinal collapse | ✅ YES | 半句 (Introduction:10) | +0.1 | LOW |
| 3. Multi-channel 提升 | ❌ NO | — | +0.05 max | MEDIUM |
| 4. Ordinal collapse 独立 contribution | ❌ NO | — | +0.05 max | HIGH |

**建议执行角度 1 + 角度 2，跳过 3 和 4。** 两处修改共 ~15 个词，零空间成本，零 overreach 风险，叙事增益清晰。

   - **Ordinal collapse**: Binary detectors (Binoculars, DetectGPT) have d1v2 AUC collapsing to 0.50 (chance) while RF maintains 0.93—key evidence that depth estimation ≠ binary detection
   - **9-cell atlas**: 3 model families (Pythia-1.4B, OLMo-1B, GPT-2 XL) × 3 decoding strategies (nucleus, temp09, topk50) × 4 depths (180K samples)
   - **Cross-strategy transfer failure**: d1-d3 balanced accuracy 45.9%; two-stage pipeline recovers to 70.5% (+11.5pp)
   - **Accumulation scenario**: 5/6 cells preserve EDD=3 at 25-50% mixing; GPT-2 XL nucleus mix50 is the sole failure (d2v3 AUC=0.695)
   - **Scale attenuation**: 14B cross-ref accuracy 44.1%, self-ref 50.8%; reference mismatch accounts for ~7pp

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

The text on which large language models are trained increasingly contains their own outputs.
As synthetic content proliferates across the web, a recursive loop emerges: models trained on web corpora ingest text generated by earlier models, and their outputs feed into the next generation's training data \cite{shumailov2024_nature,alemohammad2024_mad}.
This model$\to$data$\to$model cycle is no longer hypothetical; it is already occurring in the wild. Yet whether the recursive generation depth of a text can be estimated from its statistical properties remains unstudied, a question that matters because first-generation synthetic text may be benign or even beneficial for training, while deeply recursive text drives the distributional collapse that degrades model quality \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}.
In this work, we focus on the 1--1.5B parameter regime under \emph{controlled full-replacement chains}, where each generation fully replaces the prior training set, isolating the depth variable. Real-world contamination typically involves partial mixing (accumulation), where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions; the full-replacement setting provides an upper bound on depth signal strength, and we discuss implications for accumulation settings in \S\ref{sec:discussion}.

Existing tools address adjacent but distinct problems.
Binary detectors \cite{binoculars2024,fast_detectgpt2024,diveye2026} collapse all depths $d \geq 1$ into a single category, a limitation we confirm empirically: their pairwise d1-vs-d2 AUC collapses to chance level (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}); watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} requires proactive embedding.
The model collapse literature \cite{shumailov2024_nature,dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails} assumes depth is known a priori; \citet{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse} filter synthetic data via binary detection without distinguishing depths.
No existing method estimates the ordinal recursive generation depth of a text passage from its content alone (Figure~\ref{fig:problem}).

We find that recursive generation leaves quantifiable statistical fingerprints in text, and these fingerprints are \textbf{consistent in direction but scale-dependent in magnitude} across the three model families and three decoding strategies studied.
Specifically, the perplexity tail feature family (\texttt{p90\_ppl}, \texttt{p75\_ppl}, \texttt{kurtosis\_ppl}) and surprisal variance emerge as dominant depth indicators, with group-level dominance robust across all 9 model--strategy configurations and three importance measures.
Following the tradition of benchmark-driven empirical studies in NLP, our contribution centers on task formalization and systematic empirical characterization rather than algorithmic novelty; the convergence of four classifiers within 0.8\,pp (\S\ref{sec:gen:baselines}) confirms that discriminative signal resides in feature design, not classifier architecture.
We formalize recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification and find that a lightweight pipeline suffices: compute 19 reference-model statistical features (effective dimensionality ${\approx}$4--5 due to multicollinearity; \S\ref{sec:atlas:features}) and classify with a Random Forest into $K{+}1$ depth classes.
To characterize how recursive generation reshapes these features, we construct the \emph{Depth Degradation Atlas}: a $3 \times 3$ grid of model families $\times$ decoding strategies spanning 4 depths (180K samples).
The atlas reveals strategy-dependent degradation trajectories and we introduce \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD), to our knowledge the first operational metric for ordinal depth resolution in recursive generation, to quantify how far into the recursion chain adjacent depths remain distinguishable.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.68\textwidth]{figures/fig_problem_illustration.pdf}
\caption{Recursive generation depth estimation. A seed corpus $\mathcal{D}_0$ feeds a LoRA finetuning--sampling loop producing successively deeper corpora. Given a passage~$x$, the task is to estimate its ordinal depth~$d$.}
\label{fig:problem}
\end{figure*}
Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Task formalization and metric.} We define recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification, introduce the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric, and construct a 180K-sample benchmark ($3$ model families $\times$ $3$ decoding strategies $\times$ $4$ depths).

    \item \textbf{Depth Degradation Atlas.} The perplexity tail feature family and surprisal variance jointly dominate depth discrimination across all 9 cells; $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ in 8/9 cells (4 under nucleus depth extension), validated by 5-class extension (71--80\%); feature group ablation confirms perplexity tail dominance (76.6\% alone vs.\ 78.4\% full set).

    \item \textbf{Systematic characterization.} Cross-model transfer 66.4\% (d1--d3: 55.4\%), cross-domain arXiv 74.1\%, 14B cross-reference 44.1\% ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$); 25--50\% accumulation preserves $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}3$ in 5/6 cells despite $-$8--15\,pp accuracy attenuation. We identify cross-strategy transfer (d1--d3: 45.9\%) as a boundary condition.
\end{itemize}

\begin{abstract}
As language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises, yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification and construct a 180K-passage benchmark spanning three model families, three decoding strategies, and four depths under controlled full-replacement chains at the 1--1.5B parameter scale.
A lightweight pipeline (19 statistical features classified by Random Forest) achieves d1--d3 balanced accuracy of 59--82\% across nine model--strategy cells, with $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70} = 3$ in 8/9 cells.
Three findings emerge: (1)~depth signal concentrates in perplexity distribution tails, corroborated by classifier convergence and independent cross-perplexity features; (2)~decoding strategy affects cross-condition transfer more than model architecture, suggesting structurally distinct degradation trajectories; (3)~signal attenuates with scale (14B cross-reference accuracy ${\sim}44$\%, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}2$ for nucleus and temperature, 0 for top-$k$), with reference-model choice accounting for ${\sim}7$\,pp of the apparent degradation.
Our depth estimation claims hold most strongly within-strategy or when the decoding configuration is known.
Perturbation-based and membership-inference baselines lack ordinal depth resolution, confirming that depth estimation requires distributional statistics beyond binary detection scores.
\end{abstract}

OK, the full pipeline is:
1. Phase 2: Generate d0 (5000 samples, base model, batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=512)
2. Phase 3.1a: LoRA finetune d0 → Phase 3.1b: Generate d1
3. Phase 3.2a: LoRA finetune d1 → Phase 3.2b: Generate d2
4. Phase 3.3a: LoRA finetune d2 → Phase 3.3b: Generate d3


5. Phase 4: Feature extraction (self-reference) 
6. Phase 5: Classification (RF/LR 5-fold CV)

Running this on a single RTX PRO 6000 with 96GB memory at 7B FP16 is going to be intensive. I'm estimating the d0 generation will take around 1-1.7 hours given the batch size and token length, while each LoRA finetuning cycle should complete in roughly 0.3-0.5 hours.

For the full pipeline across all three depths, I'm looking at 4-7 hours total, plus another 1-2 hours for feature extraction and a few minutes for classification. The experiment kicked off about 11 minutes ago and is still initializing, so I'm settling in for a longer wait. While it runs, I should dig into the paper's claims more carefully—specifically which 6 cells they're referencing and whether the reported numbers actually check out.
